title: Cereon MV3 tab CDP lifecycle and correlated bounded diagnostics versus CDPilot
summary: HIGH optional diagnostic leapfrog: Cereon CdpSessionManager.registerListeners/session/dropTab owns per-tab debugger attach, one event fanout, console/network observers; CdpSession.ensureAttached/ensureDomain/markDetached retains CDP session state. NetworkObserver links request/response by requestId in capped per-tab buffers. Alternative cdpilot _FrameRoute/_frame_context_for handles same-process and cross-origin OOPIF via CDP; much larger Python browser engine, not MV3 drop-in.
aion_seam: Optional Chrome extension diagnostics and inspector behind explicit CDP permission; separate from AION P2 passive DOM observer and the sole effect Bus.
value: HIGH for optional advanced diagnostics — reduces session lifecycle, console/network capture and future frame-resolution development; not a prerequisite for I0/I1.
risks: chrome.debugger attach and broad CdpSession.send are privileged and effect-capable; CdpSession.syncDeviceMetrics calls Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride (not strictly read-only).
Chrome debugger permissions, detach/service-worker lifecycle and per-tab consent need AION decision.
Network URL/console data may be sensitive; network capture is not chat reply or conversation identity.
CDPilot OOPIF route is a 20k-line Python engine with CDP websocket/target control and effect methods, not a small TypeScript package; source/tests not executed.
acceptance: Only if Development selects: package a diagnostics-only facade with explicit grant/permission, no arbitrary CDP send from receive plane, bounded/redacted telemetry and honest detach handling; then AION-owned tests.
next_action: Development park until I1 needs diagnostics or R5 cross-frame capability; then ask Integration Manager for minimal Cereon session/observer package, using cdpilot _FrameRoute as future OOPIF reference only.
